drhp.business: E Factor Experiences is an experiential company engaged in conceptualizing, designing and executing large-scale events, experiential infrastructure and destination-based experiences, spanning cultural festivals, tourism events, multimedia shows, museums, sporting events, corporate events, eco-tourism/glamping, and proprietary intellectual properties. Its integrated service model combines creative design, technology integration, engineering-led execution and end-to-end project management, positioning it within India's experiential, tourism and cultural infrastructure ecosystem. The Company has corporate offices in New Delhi and Jaipur, with operations spanning India and overseas.
drhp.end_markets: India|overseas destinations (25 countries)|government/state tourism bodies|corporates|HNI/private clients
drhp.expansion: The Company is expanding from transient experiences into enduring cultural, civic and branded destinations. During FY26 it delivered the Maritime Heritage Museum at V.O. Chidambaranar port, Tuticorin; work was in process on museums at Wardha, Maharashtra and Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. Subsequent to year-end, it further strengthened its cultural/heritage/tourism portfolio with the Museum and Statue of Ba-Bapu & 12 Balutedar at Wardha, the Vikram Kirti Mandir Museum in Ujjain, and a permanent Immersive Experience Zone at Gandhi Park, Sri Vijaya Puram (for Andaman & Nicobar Tourism). The Company also commissioned the Shankaracharya Temple multimedia/light-projection show in Srinagar during FY26, and expanded its in-house team to over 75 professionals across specialised disciplines to support larger, more complex projects. The Company entered FY27 with its largest-ever qualified opportunity pipeline, increasingly weighted toward experiential infrastructure, museums, cultural centres and heritage redevelopment.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- India's experience economy is expanding, supported by government focus on tourism infrastructure, cultural initiatives and destination development.
- Structural shift in consumer behaviour toward immersive and experience-led consumption is driving demand.
- Government-led cultural and tourism events, corporate events and experiential marketing, social and wedding events, sports events, and destination-based experiential tourism are key growth segments for the industry.
- Growth in cultural and spiritual/religious tourism (India's religious tourism market growing from ~USD 203bn in FY24 toward ~USD 441bn by FY32) is a structural tailwind.
- Technology integration (AR/VR/AI, projection mapping) and hybrid event models are reshaping audience engagement and enabling scalable experiential formats.
- The Company entered FY27 with its largest-ever qualified opportunity pipeline, weighted toward experiential infrastructure, museums, cultural centres, heritage redevelopment and destination-led developments.
- Management indicated a qualified project pipeline exceeding Rs 500 crore entering FY27, weighted toward experiential infrastructure, museums, cultural centres, heritage redevelopment projects, immersive experiences and destination-led developments.
- Per the Managing Director's message, the opportunity pipeline entering FY27 exceeds Rs 2,500 crore, increasingly weighted towards larger and higher-value opportunities across experiential infrastructure, immersive experiences, cultural destinations and destination-led developments.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company is expanding from transient experiences into enduring cultural, civic and branded destinations. During FY26 it delivered the Maritime Heritage Museum at V.O. Chidambaranar port, Tuticorin; work was in process on museums at Wardha, Maharashtra and Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. Subsequent to year-end, it further strengthened its cultural/heritage/tourism portfolio with the Museum and Statue of Ba-Bapu & 12 Balutedar at Wardha, the Vikram Kirti Mandir Museum in Ujjain, and a permanent Immersive Experience Zone at Gandhi Park, Sri Vijaya Puram (for Andaman & Nicobar Tourism). The Company also commissioned the Shankaracharya Temple multimedia/light-projection show in Srinagar during FY26, and expanded its in-house team to over 75 professionals across specialised disciplines to support larger, more complex projects. The Company entered FY27 with its largest-ever qualified opportunity pipeline, increasingly weighted toward experiential infrastructure, museums, cultural centres and heritage redevelopment.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- brand: Recognised, IP-led immersive format — evidence: Shiva Immersive received international recognition at the World Experience Organization (WXO) Summit during London Experience Week 2026
- distribution: Long-standing vendor relations across global venues for weddings — evidence: 'backed by long-standing vendor relations across venues globally' cited in the Weddings & Social Events section
- integration: Fully in-house, self-sufficient production setup for weddings — evidence: 'a fully capable, self-sufficient in-house production setup, our evolved proprietary wedding management system'
- customer lock-in: Repeat government commissioning of large-scale cultural/tourism festivals — evidence: Maha Paryatan Utsav 2025 commissioned by Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation; Eco Retreat Odisha conceptualised and operated annually for Odisha Tourism

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Company states that macroeconomic volatility, changes in consumer spending patterns and economic slowdowns may affect demand across certain business segments.
- Execution of large-scale experiential, tourism and infrastructure projects involves coordination among multiple stakeholders and adherence to strict timelines, giving rise to operational and execution risks.
- The Company is exposed to regulatory and policy-related risks, particularly in projects involving government agencies and public institutions.
- Rapid technological advancements require continuous investment in innovation and capability enhancement to remain competitive, and increasing participation from domestic and international players may intensify competition.
- The Company remains exposed to project postponements or delays arising from geopolitical developments, adverse weather conditions and other unforeseen events, which may impact execution timelines and revenue recognition; FY26 growth was achieved despite project deferments from geopolitical developments in West Asia.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Build a diversified experiential platform spanning experiential infrastructure, destination-led tourism, immersive storytelling, cultural assets and intellectual-property-led experiences.
- Continue transformation from a project-led experiential events company into a creator of experiential infrastructure, immersive tourism, cultural destinations and IP-led experiences.
- Expand presence in higher-value and longer-duration projects that offer greater revenue visibility and recurring income potential.
- Deepen presence in high-value segments including museums, cultural centres, interpretation centres and multimedia storytelling environments.
- Build multiple engines of growth across live experiences, permanent cultural assets, destination development and intellectual properties (per Chairman's message).
- Pursue temple and pilgrimage destination redevelopment opportunities using an experience-led approach.
